sections.heading: How Our Roofing Contractors Perform Silicone Roof Coating

runs.v: Surface Preparation and Adhesion Testing

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing cleans, dries, and repairs the roof and runs an adhesion test before any field coat.

runs.v: Surface cleaning is essential for proper adhesion, and a primer is no substitute for it, per the RCMA, Gaco, and Henry, so the crew clears debris, pressure-washes off dirt, and lets the surface dry. Aged asphalt takes an epoxy primer to stop bleed-through, per Gaco.
Dry-Film Thickness and Warranty Term

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing applies high-solids silicone near 1.5 gallons per 100 square feet for roughly 22 dry mils, because warranty term scales with film thickness.

runs.v: At near 90% solids, one application reaches the specified thickness, per Gaco, Henry, and Mule-Hide, and the term runs near 10 to 15 years at 20 to 22 mils and 15 to 20 years at 30 mils, per the RCMA.
Reflectance and Surface-Temperature Reduction

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing coats for reflectance, not insulation.

runs.v: A white silicone coating starts near 0.80 to 0.88 solar reflectance and 0.85 to 0.92 emittance, per the CRRC, and reflectance drops as silicone holds dirt, to near 0.73 at 3 years for Henry Tropi-Cool; the coating adds no meaningful R-value, per the RCMA and DOE.

sections.heading: Silicone Restoration vs. Full Replacement for Aging Flat Roofs

c.v: Coat when the roof is sound underneath and only the surface has worn out; choose full replacement when water has reached the insulation or the deck.

runs.v: Newark Quality Roofing inspects the roof condition first and confirms the deck and insulation are sound, because coating over wet insulation seals the water in.

A coating candidate has a structurally sound deck, dry insulation, and a weathered but attached membrane: modified bitumen (mod bit), EPDM, TPO, built-up, metal, or spray foam. Silicone restoration reduces the need for a full tear-off by restoring the existing roof system, a professionally applied coating typically saves 50–70% of the replacement cost, and most projects are completed in 1–3 days while the building stays open.

sections.heading: How Long Does a Silicone Roof Coating Last in New Jersey's Climate?

c.v: A silicone roof coating typically lasts 10 to 20 years depending on thickness, and it extends roof life by 10–20 years over a sound roof.

runs.v: New Jersey adds summer UV exposure, ponding after storms, and dozens of freeze-thaw cycles each winter. Silicone is inherently moisture-resistant, withstands prolonged standing water without degrading, and stays flexible without cracking; its weak spot is dirt pickup, so yearly cleaning belongs in routine maintenance.

Properly maintained silicone systems can be recoated to extend their lifespan, and because silicone bonds to silicone, a roof can be recoated indefinitely without tear-off while the deck and insulation stay dry.

sections.heading: Cool Roof Coatings, ENERGY STAR, and Utility Rebates

c.v: A reflective white silicone coating makes a dark roof a cool roof, which can lower energy costs on an air-conditioned building.

runs.v: High solar reflectivity can reduce cooling costs by 15% to 30%, though Newark's heating-dominated climate trims the annual energy efficiency gain.

The EPA retired its ENERGY STAR roof program in 2022, so ratings now come from the Cool Roof Rating Council. Utility rebates change yearly; check current New Jersey programs before budgeting one. Modern high-solids silicones are low-VOC and eco-friendly.

faqs.q: Does silicone roof coating hold up in ponding water?

runs.v: Yes. 100% silicone resists permanent and standing water without softening or losing adhesion, while acrylic re-emulsifies under immersion, per the RCMA, Gaco, and Western Colloid.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace your roof?

runs.v: Restore when the deck and insulation are sound; replace when the insulation is wet or the deck is damaged, per the RCMA.

faqs.q: How long does a silicone roof coating last?

runs.v: A silicone roof coating carries a renewable 10, 15, or 20 year manufacturer warranty scaled to dry-film thickness, and is recoated with silicone at the end of the term, not torn off.

faqs.q: Does silicone roof coating lower energy costs?

runs.v: Yes, mostly in summer: a reflective white roof stays more than 50°F cooler on a sunny afternoon, per the DOE, trimming air-conditioning load. It adds no R-value.

faqs.q: Can silicone coating be recoated with acrylic later?

runs.v: No. Cured silicone is recoated with silicone; acrylic and urethane do not adhere to it, so switching chemistries requires removal first, per Gaco and the RCMA.

faqs.q: How much does silicone roof coating cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Silicone typically runs about $5.00–$9.00 per sq ft, set by roof size, dry-film thickness, and surface preparation. Newark Quality Roofing gives a free estimate in writing.

faqs.q: What standard governs silicone roof coating?

runs.v: ASTM D6694 governs liquid-applied silicone coating for spray-polyurethane-foam roofing, with a principal polymer over 95% silicone; the Cool Roof Rating Council rates reflectance under ASTM C1549.

faqs.q: How much does a 5-gallon bucket of silicone roof coating cover?

runs.v: About 330 square feet at 1.5 gallons per 100 square feet (roughly 22 dry mils), the rate Gaco and Henry specify, or about 240 square feet at a 30-mil spec. Granulated surfaces take more.

faqs.q: Which is better, silicone or elastomeric roof coating?

runs.v: Silicone is itself elastomeric; "elastomeric" on a quote usually means acrylic. On flat roofs that pond, silicone wins; acrylic, typically $3.50–$6.00 per sq ft, suits roofs that drain well.
